claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is a single-phase high-entropy alloy that can be prepared in an initially coarse-grained state.
Ultra-high-vacuum or inert testing minimizes oxidation and mixed metal-oxide film formation.
Controlled high-strain deformation can trigger localized dynamic amorphization in CoCrFeMnNi.
High-strain deformation produces an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The deformation-produced near-surface layer is amorphous.
High strain locally transforms crystalline regions into an amorphous, ultrafine structure.
The amorphous or ultrafine surface structure increases dislocation pinning.
The deformation-induced surface structure increases shear strength.
Predominantly coarse-grained crystalline material permits easier dislocation motion.
Easier dislocation motion in the less-deformed crystalline material results in lower hardness.
Specimens containing the deformation-induced amorphous surface layer will be significantly harder than minimally deformed specimens.
Specimens containing the deformation-induced near-surface layer will have lower friction coefficients than minimally deformed specimens.
A lower friction coefficient indicates enhanced yield strength.
Dynamic amorphization governs enhanced hardness and strength in single-phase high-entropy alloys.
The proposed mechanism should extend to single-phase high-entropy alloys with compositions and microstructures similar to CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to multiphase alloys.
Surface oxidation or other reactive processes can interfere with formation of the proposed amorphous layer.
The critical strain, strain-rate, and grain-size thresholds for dynamic amorphization have not been precisely determined.

contradictions.description: The layer is repeatedly described as both amorphous and ultra-nanocrystalline. A fully amorphous phase has no crystalline grains, so the hypothesis must distinguish an amorphous layer from a nanocrystalline layer or specify a mixed amorphous–nanocrystalline structure.
